mathcounts-potw-2026-05-04-01.title: Parts of the ratio
mathcounts-potw-2026-05-04-01.body:
Total shirts: $224 + 56 + 152 = 432$. Ratio parts: $5 + 11 + 6 + 2 = 24$, so one part is $432 \div 24 = 18$. Medium: $11 \times 18 = 198$.

**Answer: 198**

mathcounts-potw-2026-05-04-02.title: Work from 4 ribbons down
mathcounts-potw-2026-05-04-02.body:
- **4 ribbons:** 2 people (V, S, M, T).
- **3 ribbons:** 5 people have S and M; 2 are the 4-ribbon people, so 3 have exactly V, S, M. These are the only 3 people with 3 ribbons.
- **2 ribbons** (V + one other): Monitors: $7 - 5 = 2$ with V, M. Scorers: $12 - 5 = 7$ with V, S. Timers who are Monitors: just the 2 four-ribbon people, so 2 Timers are not Monitors; they can't have 3 ribbons, so they have V, T. Total $2 + 7 + 2 = 11$.
- **Multiple ribbons:** $2 + 3 + 11 = 16$. **One ribbon:** $2 \times 16 = 32$.

Total: $16 + 32 = 48$.

**Answer: 48**

mathcounts-potw-2026-05-04-02.title: Venn-diagram bookkeeping
mathcounts-potw-2026-05-04-02.body:
Since everyone has V, look only at S, M, T. Regions: SMT = 2; exactly two of S, M, T = 3 people, and all must be SM (because S∩M has 5 = 2 + 3), so ST-only = MT-only = 0. Then M only $= 7 - 5 = 2$, S only $= 12 - 5 = 7$, T∩M $= 2$ so T only $= 2$. People with at least one of S, M, T: $2 + 3 + 2 + 7 + 2 = 16$; people with V only: 32. Total 48.

**Answer: 48**

mathcounts-potw-2026-05-04-03.title: Count by length
mathcounts-potw-2026-05-04-03.body:
A must answer the last question and have exactly 2 earlier correct answers.
- 3 questions: AAA — 1 way.
- 4 questions: one B among the first 3 — 3 ways.
- 5 questions: two Bs among the first 4 — $\binom42 = 6$ ways.

Total $1 + 3 + 6 = 10$.

**Answer: 10**

mathcounts-potw-2026-05-04-03.title: List them all
mathcounts-potw-2026-05-04-03.body:
B can get 0, 1 or 2 questions before A's third correct answer:
- AAA
- BAAA, ABAA, AABA
- BBAAA, BABAA, BAABA, ABBAA, ABABA, AABBA

That is 10 ways.

**Answer: 10**
